activityData.title: Equivalent fractions check
activityData.instructions: Choose the best answer for each question. Use the hint if you need a nudge.
activityData.subject: Maths

feedback.generalCorrect: You are matching fractions by their value, not just by how they look.
feedback.generalIncorrect: Check whether the fractions describe the same sized part of the same whole.

activityData.teacherNotes: This activity deliberately moves from conceptual recognition to symbolic reasoning.

introductoryMedia.altText: Two fraction bars show that one half and two quarters shade the same amount.
introductoryMedia.caption: One half and two quarters can represent the same amount of the same whole.

questions.prompt: A bar is split into 2 equal parts and 1 part is shaded. Which fraction shows the same amount?
questions.supportingText: Think about the same whole being divided into more equal parts.

media.altText: A visual comparison shows one half has the same shaded length as two quarters.
media.caption: Compare the shaded part in each bar.

media.altText: The two quarters option shows two out of four equal parts shaded.
media.caption: Two quarters

questions.hint: One half is the same as two out of four equal parts.
questions.correctFeedback: Yes. If each half is split into two, one half becomes two quarters.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Not quite. Compare the amount shaded, not just the denominator.
questions.explanation: 1/2 and 2/4 cover the same amount of the whole.

questions.correctFeedback: Correct. 3 out of 6 equal parts is half of the whole.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Look at the relationship between the numerator and denominator in 3/6.
questions.explanation: 3/6 simplifies to 1/2 because both numbers can be divided by 3.

questions.prompt: Which two fractions are equivalent to 2/3?
questions.supportingText: There may be more than one correct answer.
questions.hint: Multiply the numerator and denominator by the same number.
questions.correctFeedback: Good reasoning. 2/3 can become 4/6 or 6/9 by scaling both parts equally.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Equivalent fractions need the numerator and denominator changed by the same factor.

questions.hint: The denominator has been multiplied by 2.
questions.correctFeedback: Yes. If 5 is multiplied by 2 to make 10, 4 must also be multiplied by 2.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Use the same multiplier for the numerator as for the denominator.

questions.prompt: Sam says 3/4 is equivalent to 6/12 because both numbers got bigger. What should you say?

options.text: Sam is correct because bigger numbers always make an equivalent fraction.
Sam is incorrect because 3 and 4 were not multiplied by the same number.
Sam is correct because 6/12 is more than 3/4.

questions.hint: Check the multiplier from 3 to 6 and from 4 to 12.
questions.correctFeedback: Exactly. 3 was doubled, but 4 was tripled, so the fractions are not equivalent.
questions.incorrectFeedback: Equivalent fractions must scale the numerator and denominator by the same factor.
questions.explanation: 3/4 would become 6/8 if both parts were multiplied by 2.
